Darth Krayt — feat/statement extraction from Wookieepedia

Scope: article body through “Notes and references”; navigation, trivia, appearances, sources, and reference lists omitted. Quotations below are copied from the article. “Statement/hype” labels preserve the article’s own framing and are not presented as objective feats.

OPENING SUMMARY / BIOGRAPHICAL OVERVIEW

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: opening biography. “When he was only a teen, Hett's father was murdered by the Ex-Jedi turned assassin Aurra Sing, who was later defeated in a duel by a young A'Sharad Hett.” Scaling: the article identifies Sing as the ex-Jedi assassin who killed Hett’s father; the detailed early-life section says Hett was still a Padawan and that his father, a fully trained Jedi Knight, had been unable to defeat Sing.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: opening biography. “During the Clone Wars, he served the Republic as a General and established himself as a charismatic leader who often led his troops from the front.” Scaling/context: the article names the Battle of Boz Pity and Siege of Saleucami as key conflicts and says he survived the Clone Wars and was one of the few Jedi known to have escaped the Great Jedi Purge.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: opening biography. “However, during a skirmish on Had Abbadon, Krayt was stabbed, electrocuted, and sent hurtling off a cliff. The Sith Lord's powers proved strong, however, when they saved his life.” Scaling/context: this is before the later murder and resurrection; the detailed account says he cushioned the fall with the Force after Azlyn Rae’s stab and Morne/Muur’s lightning and Force-push.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Reborn feat] Section: opening biography. “Krayt later healed his body from his death experience.” Scaling/context: the later Resurrection section specifies that he healed himself of his Yuuzhan Vong implants; after rebirth he retook Coruscant and slew Darth Wyyrlok.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Reborn feat] Section: opening biography. “With the aid of loyal Sith and a new breed of Sith troopers, Krayt retook Coruscant, slaying Darth Wyyrlok in the process.” Scaling/context: the later Resurrection section describes a short, intense duel in which Krayt impaled Wyyrlok through the chest.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Final death] Section: opening biography. “However, in the final battle, he once again attempted to turn Cade Skywalker. He failed to do so, and while distracted in the attempt was slain by Cade, who incinerated his corpse to prevent the ghost of Krayt from simply resurrecting his dead body.”
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

BIOGRAPHY — PRE-REBIRTH / A’SHARAD HETT

[Statement] Section: Pre-birth. “Prior to 67 BBY, Darth Krayt was foreseen by the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Tenebrous, who predicted through calculations with his enormous brain that the future of the Sith would see eventually the arrival of a ‘One Sith’ with no need of a replacement and rule forever, naively believing it would be him, although those predictions veered more towards Darth Sidious' rise to power.” Scaling/context: this is Tenebrous’s prediction, not a demonstrated Krayt feat.
  Source: "The Tenebrous Way" — Star Wars Insider 130 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 16; exact text match]

[Feat] Section: Early life (47 BBY–22 BBY). “He once undertook the ritual of slaying a krayt dragon.”
  Source: Star Wars: Outlander [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 1; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Becoming a Knight. “However, during the fight, A'Sharad used his anger to overcome Sing, and was able to knock her unconscious.” Scaling/context: Sing was his father’s killer and the article calls the fight a deadly duel; Hett regained control and did not kill her, instead turning her over to Ki-Adi-Mundi and the other Jedi Masters.
  Source: Star Wars: The Hunt for Aurra Sing [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 11; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth achievement] Section: Becoming a Knight. “Over the course of the next decade, A'Sharad managed to complete his training under the guidance of the Dark Woman, and ascended to the rank of Jedi Knight.”
  Source: Republic 59 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 4; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The Clone Wars (22 BBY–19 BBY). “During the Clone Wars, A'Sharad served as a General for the Galactic Republic, and flew his Jedi starfighter in air support as part of Zeta Squadron during the Battle of Geonosis.” Scaling/context: the article also says he led clone troopers on Metalorn and Aargonar.
  Source: Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 19; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The Clone Wars. “In the heat of his rage, Anakin even tried to attack A'Sharad, but the elder Jedi, though without a lightsaber, defended himself, and managed to disarm the younger Jedi.” Scaling/context: Anakin had just slaughtered enemy soldiers while imagining them to be the Sand People who had tortured his mother; Hett then revealed he was human and kept Anakin’s confession secret.
  Source: UNSOURCED on Wookieepedia (sentence found in "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608 but it has no inline citation in its paragraph; exact text match)

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The Clone Wars. “In 19 BBY, A'Sharad went with many other Jedi to Boz Pity to assist General Kenobi and General Skywalker in their hunt for Separatist and Sith leaders. The Jedi were ambushed by Lord Dooku and General Grievous. A'Sharad fought with his lightsaber and augmented himself to be able to punch down B-1s during this battle.” Scaling/context: the next sentence says that, with his help, the Jedi defeated the Sith and droids in the battle.
  Source: Obsession 4 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 20; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The Clone Wars. “On Saleucami, A'Sharad flew for the Republic, working together with his friend, Xiaan Amersu, to destroy the Separatist's planetary gun, but Xiaan was forced to sacrifice herself, crashing her ruined starfighter into the enemy, to destroy their target.” Scaling/context: the article says the Republic eventually succeeded and Hett survived the campaign.
  Source: Star Wars: Republic: Siege of Saleucami [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 18; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth achievement] Section: The Clone Wars. “At some point by the end of the Clone Wars, A'Sharad attained the rank of Jedi Master.”
  Source: Legacy — War 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 22; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Post-Clone Wars—Return to Tatooine. “Hett killed the clones assigned to execute him, keeping one alive just long enough to learn what had happened.” Scaling/context: this was during Order 66; he was away from his troops on a scouting mission and saw other Jedi die.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 16 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 23; approximate match 0.97, verify]

[Pre-rebirth achievement] Section: Post-Clone Wars—Return to Tatooine. “Hett led these clans against human settlements that had encroached on Tusken lands, while at the same time silently preparing for his own private war against the Galactic Empire.” Scaling/context: the article says his leadership and Clone Wars skills reversed Tusken losses, and the Tuskens became a feared fighting force again and reclaimed land.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 16 ; The New Essential Chronology [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 23,24; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: A'Sharad Hett vs. Obi-Wan Kenobi. “With little choice, both Jedi ignited their lightsabers and fought a brutal duel on the desert flat, with the entire Tusken army watching them.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 16 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 23; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth loss / scaling] Section: A'Sharad Hett vs. Obi-Wan Kenobi. “The duel ended with the loss of Hett's right arm, and the extra humiliation of having his mask removed.” Scaling/context: the article says Kenobi would not kill him, instead forcing him to leave Tatooine; Hett had been close to the dark side and was fighting Kenobi without yet being a Sith.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 16 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 23; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Post-Clone Wars. “While pursuing a bounty named Resk to the Sith home planet of Korriban, a storm forced them down, and Hett continued his pursuit of Resk. Hett killed him after Resk threatened to turn him over to the authorities when Hett revealed himself to have been a Jedi.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 17 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 9; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The rise of Darth Krayt. “Shortly after Vergere left him to join with the main invasion force, Hett escaped and destroyed the scout ship, and returned to Korriban.” Scaling/context: he had been captured by the Yuuzhan Vong, imprisoned in the Embrace of Pain, tortured, subjected to Shaper experiments, and unable to sense the Vong in the Force.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 18 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 7; exact text match]

[Statement] Section: The rise of Darth Krayt. “On Korriban, Hett took the name Darth Krayt, after the fearsome krayt dragon of his homeworld, and reestablished the Sith under his leadership, pledging to reunify the galaxy according to his will.”
  Source: Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Special Edition ; Legacy (2006) 18 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 26,7; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The rise of Darth Krayt. “Instead, there would be the Rule of One—that one being the Sith Order itself, under which there would be many members under the direction of a single Dark Lord of the Sith.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 18 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 7; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The rise of Darth Krayt. “By the year 41 ABY, Darth Krayt tried to undermine the Jedi with a clone of Jaden Korr, apprentice of Jedi Master Kyle Katarn: but this would ultimately fail.” Marked as an attempted operation, not a successful feat.
  Source: Riptide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 27; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The rise of Darth Krayt. “During this time of hiding, Krayt was able to keep his operations, and grand displays of the Force, hidden from the Jedi and even other Sith, to the point that Luke Skywalker, Ben Skywalker, and Vestara Khai (and the hounds under her control) could not find the One Sith.” Scaling/context: the article also says he inserted spies into the New Jedi Order.
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Ascension [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 28; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Abeloth. “When she tried to take him into custody after sensing his dark side aura, he disarmed her before telling her: ‘Not yet, Jedi. Abeloth first.’” Scaling/context: Luke Skywalker ordered that the unknown Sith Master not be attacked so long as he did not interfere, because the Jedi did not need another foe.
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 29; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat, with Luke] Section: Abeloth. “Both Krayt and Skywalker ultimately managed to defeat Abeloth, thanks to her host bodies being destroyed around the same time, but the two were left gravely injured, though still alive.” Scaling/context: Krayt fought alongside Grand Master Luke Skywalker; Luke initially thought Krayt might be a Lost Tribe Sith but later recognized he was a separate Sith Lord.
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse ; Legacy (2006) 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 29,8; exact text match]

[Statement / prediction] Section: Abeloth. “In addition, when Luke explained that the Sith would not gain the Throne of Balance due to foreseeing a Jedi Queen, Krayt implied that the future of a Sith-dominated Throne of Balance was only delayed and not actually averted, correctly predicting he would one day rule the galaxy.” This is a character prediction/statement, not a standalone feat.
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse ; Legacy (2006) 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 29,8; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: Abeloth. “Decades after the fight with Abeloth, Krayt slew a Devaronian Jedi and their partner. Krayt kidnapped their daughter, Malincha and trained her as a Sith.” Scaling/context: Malincha became Darth Maladi, head of the One Sith’s intelligence and assassination branch.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 45 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 14; exact text match]

THE SITH–IMPERIAL WAR AND PRE-REBIRTH RULE

[Achievement] Section: The Sith–Imperial War. “At last, in the period of 127–130 ABY, the Sith made their presence known openly under Krayt's leadership, and the result of his machinations was the Sith–Imperial War.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 8 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 30; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The Sith–Imperial War. “Krayt sabotage a Jedi project that was established for entirely altruistic reasons.” Scaling/context: the article describes the Ossus Project’s Yuuzhan Vong terraforming as successful before Krayt’s apprentice Darth Maladi and rogue Shaper Zenoc Quah sabotaged it with a Vongspawn virus.
  Source: Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 31; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The Sith–Imperial War. “The results were everything he could have hoped for.” Scaling/context: the article says the sabotage caused resentment toward the Yuuzhan Vong, the Empire invoked the Treaty of Anaxes and declared war on the Galactic Alliance, and divided Alliance worlds made it easy to conquer.
  Source: Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 31; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The Sith–Imperial War. “In three years, the Galactic Alliance was forced into surrender and the Empire absorbed all its former holdings, even reclaiming Coruscant as the Imperial throneworld.” Scaling/context: the article calls this a reversal of the galactic order and says it was a stepping stone for Krayt.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 8 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 30; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The consolidation of power. “Krayt dispatched his Hand, Darth Nihl, on a devastating attack against the praxeum. However, what came to be known as the Massacre at Ossus was not the absolute victory he hoped for.” Scaling/context: Nihl killed prominent Jedi including Kol Skywalker; the Jedi were scattered, not defeated.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 8; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: The consolidation of power. “He launched a daring palace revolution, marching with his cohorts straight into the audience chamber of Emperor Roan Fel himself, killing the man who sat on the throne, and seating himself in his place.” Scaling/context: the article says the slain Emperor was a double and that the real Fel was a fully trained Imperial Knight who would have defended himself.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 8; exact text match]

[Statement / self-characterization] Section: The consolidation of power. “The galaxy writhes in chaos and disorder. It requires a man of vision. I am that man of vision. I am the new Emperor.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 8; exact text match]

[Achievement] Section: The consolidation of power. “Krayt ruled his new Empire as the leader of both the One Sith and the Council of Moffs. He also was the Sith Lord who held dominion over Coruscant and the commander of the Coruscant Defense Fleet.”
  Source: Legacy Era Campaign Guide [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 32; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth setback] Section: Discovery. “Maleval was shot down by Anson Trask, and Kruhl was shot and killed by Emperor Fel on Bastion.” Scaling/context: these were Krayt’s minions sent to destroy the 908th Stormtrooper Division and eliminate Emperor Fel.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 4 ; Legacy (2006) 13 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 37,38; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Skywalker found. “Krayt then took Cade to his chambers alongside Darth Talon and Darth Wyyrlok, leaving both Lady Maladi and Lord Nihl outside.” Scaling/context: he had first sensed Cade heading to rescue Jedi Hosk Trey’lis and tasked Nihl and Talon with capturing him; they did so.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 15 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 25; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Skywalker found. “Krayt was astonished to see Cade's body had purged itself of the deadly substances Maladi had injected into his body.” Scaling/context: Krayt then ordered Maladi to infect Jariah Syn and Deliah Blue with deadly Yorik-Kul coral seeds so he could witness Cade’s power; Cade saved them.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 15 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 25; approximate match 1.00, verify]

[Pre-rebirth combat feat] Section: Skywalker found. “When Cade succeeded in cutting off Nihl's right arm, Krayt commanded him to kill the Sith Lord.” Scaling/context: Cade refused and began a duel with Krayt; Krayt was almost defeating Cade before Morrigan Corde shot Krayt in the back.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 19 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 41; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth statement] Section: Genocide. “Ten percent of the Mon Calamari population are to be executed. Effective immediately. We will start with the Mon Calamari at hand.” Scaling/context: he had Gial Gahan and other Mon Calamari murdered, ordered the rest interned in work camps, and ordered the entire Mon Calamari Council executed. The article says the resulting fear strengthened him through the dark side but triggered resistance.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 22 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 43; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth combat / survival feat] Section: Betrayer of the dream. “At the bottom of the cliff, Darth Wyyrlok, having landed his shuttle nearby, approached the Emperor's body, declaring that he would be taken to the tomb of the Sith on Korriban. To his surprise, Krayt woke, having cushioned his fall with the Force.” Scaling/context: this followed Azlyn Rae’s stab, Morne/Muur’s lightning and Force-push, and the cliff fall; Wyyrlok then electrocuted him.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 31 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 2; exact text match]

REBIRTH / RESURRECTION

[Reborn feat] Section: Resurrection. “He had also healed himself of his Yuuzhan Vong implants which he had foreseen as part of his rebirth.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 48 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 52; exact text match]

[Reborn achievement] Section: Resurrection. “For decades he had taken the most powerful, newly-born Force-sensitives, having them enhanced with cybernetic implants and turned into unquestionably loyal Sith troopers that would take their own lives when ordered to do so by their master.” Scaling/context: he paired these troopers with a new, more powerful class of Sith starfighter as part of his plan to become unquestioned leader of the galaxy.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 50 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 15; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Resurrection. “He had also healed himself of his Yuuzhan Vong implants which he had foreseen as part of his rebirth.” The article also says he revealed his will and presence to all beings in the galaxy who had ever touched the dark side, including Cade Skywalker.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 48 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 52; exact text match]

[Reborn combat feat] Section: Resurrection. “After a short, but intense duel, Darth Krayt led Wyyrlok to believe he was victorious, only to then impale the usurper through the chest.” Scaling/context: Wyyrlok had previously murdered Krayt and had claimed that this Krayt was an impostor; Krayt regained control of the Empire and Sith.
  Source: Legacy — War 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 22; exact text match]

[Statement] Section: Resurrection. “The Galaxy must experience the pain of death and rapture of rebirth as I have. I will bring chaos. It is time for war.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 50 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 15; exact text match]

WAR / REBORN FEATS

[Reborn achievement] Section: War. “After taking back control of the Empire and the Sith, Darth Krayt led the Empire into the offensive, to teach the Galaxy the meaning of fear, and the recklessness of incurring his wrath.” Scaling/context: the article lists the fall of Vinsoth, the bombing of Falleen for refusing to ally with him, and Borosk returning to Sith Imperial control.
  Source: Legacy — War 2 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 53; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: War. “Later, Krayt's Sith Inquisitor, Darth Havok, successfully tortured the location of the hidden Jedi temple out of the imprisoned Antares Draco.” Scaling/context: Krayt ordered Talon to find Cade and make him a gift of the broken Imperial Knight; he continued to believe Cade would serve him.
  Source: Legacy — War 2 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 53; exact text match]

[Reborn strategic feat] Section: Battle of Taivas. “Despite the Moffs' disbelief, Krayt remained unfazed and unsurprised.” Scaling/context: the article says the Jedi, Galactic Alliance Remnant, and Roan Fel’s loyalists had laid a trap and ambushed the Sith-Imperial fleet.
  Source: Legacy — War 3 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 55; exact text match]

[Reborn strategic/combat result] Section: Battle of Taivas. “The intervention of the Sith army turned the tide of the battle due to their willingness to kill both allies and Imperials.” Scaling/context: Moff Geist was killed by friendly fire; Moff Yage defected; Krayt’s side suffered massive losses but robbed the allies of victory, weakened the Moffs, damaged Alliance morale, and gained troops for an assault on Bastion.
  Source: Legacy — War 4 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 54; exact text match]

[Reborn combat feat] Section: Ultimate death. “Krayt began their final confrontation by pushing Skywalker away with the Force before unleashing a barrage of Force lightning and the two engaged in battle.” Scaling/context: Krayt said he was much more powerful than in their previous encounter; they then clashed blades.
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Reborn feat / technique] Section: Ultimate death. “Krayt's skill was great, however, and revealed that by experiencing death, Cade had shown him the mechanism of dark transfer.”
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Ultimate death. “Using the power on its creator, Krayt caused Skywalker to die, before resurrecting him, and there Cade Skywalker saw Krayt's vision of the future.” Scaling/context: the vision showed Coruscant burning, Cade’s friends dead, and Cade enthralled in a Sith body; Krayt said the Sith were immune to Omega Red.
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Reborn defeat] Section: Ultimate death. “Cade Skywalker then immediately summoned his lightsaber and in a flash, leaped around and pierced his lightsaber into Krayt's heart, killing him, and declaring himself a Jedi.” Scaling/context: the article says Krayt was distracted while trying to turn Cade.
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Final-death prevention] Section: Ultimate death. “Knowing that Krayt's body would simply heal itself again and return from death once more, and feeling Krayt's spirit prying into his mind, Cade asked his mother for her ship, intending to fly it into Coruscant Prime to destroy both himself and Krayt's body.”
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Statement / threat] Section: Ultimate death. “Krayt smirked that if his body was destroyed, he would use Cade's body to return, having learned essence transfer from Darth Andeddu and Karness Muur.” Scaling/context: the article says Cade escaped before the ship collided with the sun and Krayt’s corpse was incinerated; afterward Krayt’s spirit ceased troubling Cade.
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Post-death legacy statement] Section: Legacy. “The One Sith, however, survived the loss of its founder and planned to continue Krayt's plans to subjugate the galaxy under Sith dominance, but decided on going about it in a different approach.”
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

POWERS AND ABILITIES — LIGHTSABER / MARTIAL ARTS

[Statement / claim] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “I completed my training as both Jedi and Sith. I honed my skills during the Clone Wars and have killed thousands of opponents since then.” —Darth Krayt to Cade Skywalker. Marked as Krayt’s own claim, not independently verified by the article.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 19 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 61; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth scaling feat] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “A'Sharad Hett was exceptionally skilled in the NIman Jar'Kai style of lightsaber combat.” Scaling/context: the article says he defeated Aurra Sing while still a Padawan, despite his fully trained Jedi Knight father having been unable to defeat her; it also says Hett’s power was augmented by hatred and that he used Force rage.
  Source: Star Wars: Republic: Siege of Saleucami [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 18; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “He, while holding back, defeated the Dark Woman in a duel.” Scaling/context: the article says she then subdued him with a sneak attack after the duel was formally over to teach him not to lower his guard.
  Source: Star Wars (1998) 13 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 62; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “Hett killed a Krayt dragon with a Gaderffii and a torch before he was officially made a Jedi.”
  Source: Star Wars: Outlander [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 1; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “During the Clone Wars, he defeated an enraged (and armed with a lightsaber) Anakin Skywalker while armed with only a gaderffii. Then he made peace with the Chosen One.”
  Source: Republic 59 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 65; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “Later, while part of a Jedi and Clone force, he and his friends were able to drive off the ambush of Separatist forces that were led by the Sith Lord Count Dooku and General Grievous.” Scaling/context: this is the article’s stated connection to Dooku and Grievous; it does not say Hett defeated either leader in a one-on-one duel.
  Source: Obsession 5 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 21; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat / loss] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “After turning to the dark side, but before becoming a Sith Lord, Hett engaged the extremely powerful Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi (who had a few years before defeated Darth Vader) in a lightsaber duel and proved capable of holding his own against Kenobi even to the point of striking him with the hilt of his blade and kicking him, but was eventually defeated and maimed.” Scaling: the comparison to Kenobi’s earlier defeat of Vader is stated by the article; the article records Hett’s eventual defeat here.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 16 ; Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 23,66; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat with Luke / Abeloth scaling] Section: Lightsaber and Martial Arts Skills. “Krayt was able to survive the battle and beat, rend, bash, and grapple her, causing massive damage to Abeloth, and alongside his draining of her power, caused her to be unable to keep her other avatars functioning elsewhere.” Scaling/context: he was aided by Luke Skywalker and the article says they ultimately “killed” Abeloth.

FORCE POWERS — OVERALL SCALING AND TELEKINESIS

[Statement / hype] Section: Force Powers. “As the Dark Lord of the One Sith, Darth Krayt was the strongest Sith Lord of his time.” Scaling/context: the article immediately calls him “one of the most capable that ever lived”; this is an article assessment, not a discrete feat.

[Statement / comparison] Section: Force Powers. “In 40 ABY, the Jedi Grandmaster Luke was troubled with visions of Krayt as a shadowy figure who seemed at least as ruthless and strong in the Force as the Chosen One, seeming like a dark spirit on a mission of doom.” Marked as Luke’s visions/comparison, not an objective feat.
  Source: Legacy of the Force: Betrayal ; Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 60,29; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat with Luke] Section: Force Powers. “The Dark Lord was powerful enough in the Force to battle a being as powerful as Abeloth, though he was assisted by Grand Master Luke Skywalker, who himself was wary of dueling Krayt in beyond shadows, even to the point of almost backstabbing the Sith preemptively.”
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 29; exact text match]

[Statement / character belief] Section: Force Powers. “Jacen Solo believed that if Krayt acquired Allana Solo as an apprentice that Krayt would become unstoppable and usher in an appalling new future.” Marked as Jacen’s belief.
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 29; exact text match]

[Statement] Section: Force Powers. “The Force itself was bent to Krayt's will.” The article also says the darkness brought on by his rise made it harder than ever for Jedi masters to use the Force to sense the future; these are broad article statements/hype.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 68; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Force Powers. “Krayt's strength in the dark side was great enough to be felt by every Sith in the galaxy.” Scaling/context: the article says he claimed his power multiplied after resurrection and that the dark side seemed to live through him.
  Source: Legacy (2006) 50 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 15; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Force Powers. “His strength in the dark side was such that he could fight and overpower Cade Skywalker, who was armed with a lightsaber, with mostly his usage of the Force alone.”
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat] Section: Force Powers. “A'Sharad Hett possessed incredible skill in telekinesis, as shown when able to non-lethally repulse a mob of his fellow Tuskans who were harassing Mundi, a feat that impressed the Jedi Master, though was seen as possibly too violent for the situation.”
  Source: Star Wars (1998) 11 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 57; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat with Luke / Abeloth] Section: Force Powers. “As a Dark Lord in 44 ABY he showed continued mastery of this skill, such as when he disarmed a Jedi, then later yanked Abeloth back to himself and Luke via recalling his embedded severed hand and thus effectively countering her teleportation, as the attack caused her very essence to leak from her wounds.”

[Reborn feat] Section: Force Powers. “Krayt threw Maladi to the ground without expressing significant effort, made officials kneel before him, disciplined Darth Nihl in the Valley of the Dark Lords by briefly Force choking him, and he redirected multiple stones thrown at him by Darth Wyyrlok after holding the barrage in stasis.” Scaling/context: when Krayt released the rocks, Wyyrlok had to raise a Force bubble to avoid death.

FORCE LIGHTNING / DURABILITY / PRECOGNITION

HEALING, DARK TRANSFER, AND ESSENCE TRANSFER

[Pre-rebirth statement] Section: Force Powers. “Before turning to the dark side, A'Sharad Hett was trained to use Force healing, though the extent of his healing abilities is unknown.”
  Source: Republic 58 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 12; exact text match]

[Pre-rebirth feat with Luke / Abeloth] Section: Force Powers. “When Abeloth cut off his hand beyond shadows, a wound that would have normally transferred over to his physical form, he reclaimed and restored the hand.” Scaling/context: the article compares this with Luke Skywalker, who was left with lasting wounds from similar blows.
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse ; Legacy (2006) 30 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 29,47; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Force Powers. “However, after the Battle of Had Abbadon, Darth Krayt was finally able to completely heal himself of his Yuuzhan Vong growths as well as what would normally be severe mortal wounds, demonstrating that his skill in Force Healing had greatly increased, and also worthy of note due to the fact that the Yuuzhan Vong were almost impossible to touch with the Force, save with lightning.”
  Source: Legacy (2006) 18 ; Legacy (2006) 48 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 7,52; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Force Powers. “While before the battle his power over death had been limited to resisting aging, now he was able to wield the Force to resurrect his own corpse post-mortem.”
  Source: Star Wars: Beware the Sith ; Legacy Era Campaign Guide ; Legacy (2006) 48 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 92,32,52; exact text match]

[Reborn feat / dark transfer] Section: Force Powers. “During his final duel with Cade Skywalker, Krayt revealed that when he experienced death on Had Abbadon, he discovered the rare dark side power of dark transfer, allowing him to return from death itself and explosively augment his already considerable healing powers--even to the point of restoring his withered flesh to a fit and strong state.”
  Source: Legacy — War 6 ; Legacy — War 1 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3,22; exact text match]

[Reborn feat] Section: Force Powers. “Darth Krayt could also use Dark Transfer in tandem with Force Lightning to injure or kill such as when he killed and resurrected Cade Skywalker during their final duel, much like how Cade himself used his Dark Transfer.”

[Statement / threat] Section: Force Powers. “From beyond the grave, the Sith Lord taunted Cade Skywalker that his proficiency with Dark Transfer advanced to the degree in which he would heal himself even from death itself, according to the testimony of Cade Skywalker.”
  Source: Legacy — War 6 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Krayt" rev 15688608, ref 3; exact text match]

[Statement / threat] Section: Force Powers. “After his final death, Krayt's spirit claimed that he learned the dangerous art of essence transfer and threatened to return to life within Cade Skywalker if his body was destroyed.” Scaling/context: the article says this threat ended after Krayt’s body was burned.
